D018-D005_h001.question:
Lately, things have been really tough, Dr. I'm 19, a culinary student, and it feels like my life is just falling apart. I can't even enjoy cooking anymore, and that used to be my passion. Nothing brings me joy, not even the smell of fresh bread or the taste of something delicious I've made. It's like a gray cloud has moved in and stolen all the color. I keep thinking back to… it was a really bad experience, and I just blame myself for everything that happened. If only I had done things differently, maybe it wouldn't have.

And then there's the anger. It’s always there, a simmering pot inside me, ready to boil over, and sometimes it does. I snap at people for no reason. It's also hard to focus on anything, especially during lectures or when I'm trying to read a recipe. My mind just drifts, and I can't concentrate for more than a few minutes. And the noises! Every sudden sound makes me jump out of my skin, my heart races like crazy. The other day, a plate dropped in the kitchen, and I practically hit the ceiling.

But the weirdest thing is, I keep hearing voices. They tell me to do things, bad things sometimes, or just whisper my name from afar when no one’s there. It’s not like they're talking about *that* specific event though; they’re completely separate, just… there. And sometimes I see things in my peripheral vision, shadows moving, even though I know logically there's nothing there. It’s all so confusing and scary.
D018-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h002.question:
Lately, everything just feels… grey. Like someone sucked all the color out of the world. Nothing makes me happy anymore, not even the old shows I used to love. And my memory's gone to pot; I'm constantly misplacing equipment or forgetting calls. It's frustrating, and honestly, it makes me furious. I find myself lashing out a lot, especially at dispatch, feeling like they're always setting me up for failure. It all started after that multi-car pileup last year. Every time I get a new call, or even just hear a siren, my stomach knots up and my heart races.

But it's not just that. Sometimes, even when it's quiet, I hear whispers, faint voices calling my name from the corners of the room. They say strange, unsettling things that have nothing to do with what I’ve seen on the job. And the shadows… they seem to move out of the corner of my eye. It’s like something else is happening, something beyond just the bad memories.
D018-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h003.question:
Lately, things have been really tough, doc. It's like my mind is playing tricks on me. I see shadows moving in my peripheral vision, and sometimes I hear whispers, especially when I'm alone in the garage. They’re not saying anything specific, just a constant murmur. It’s not about the accident at work last year, the beam falling, or anything like that. That’s still there, in my thoughts, those flashes of the crane giving way. But these other things, they’re just... there, on their own.

I just don't feel anything good anymore. My wife tries, but I can't even get excited about our son's soccer games. It’s hard to concentrate; my thoughts feel all muddled, like I’m in a fog. The other day, my boy just touched my arm to get my attention and I jumped out of my skin, almost knocking over my coffee. And I keep replaying that accident from the shop, kicking myself for not checking the hoist one last time. I feel this deep shame, like I let everyone down. But these whispers… they definitely aren’t about that.
D018-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h004.question:
It’s been months now, probably close to eight, and honestly, running the restaurant feels impossible. I used to love it, but now I can barely bring myself to care. My husband, bless his heart, keeps asking what’s wrong, but I just… I don’t know. Every so often, I’ll be trying to order supplies or something mundane, and I’ll just get hit with these flashes – vivid, horrible memories of the robbery, like it's happening all over again. I’ll start shaking, my heart pounding, and it takes forever for me to calm down.

It’s not just the memories, though. Lately, I've been hearing things, whispers mostly, sometimes full conversations. They don’t have anything to do with the robbery, which is strange. I don’t recognize the voices, and they often talk about things no one else seems to notice. I keep wondering if our landlord is sabotaging us, or maybe that new delivery driver; someone has to be responsible for all this. Even picking out what to wear in the morning feels like an insurmountable task. The initial shock and terror from that night, it just… hasn't faded. It’s like it’s still right here, in my chest, all the time. And these voices, they're definitely not helping.
D018-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h005.question: It's been about seven months now. I keep having these awful dreams, always the same scenario of the accident, waking up in a cold sweat. During the day, it's just… flat. Nothing brings me joy anymore, not even my husband, which makes me feel even worse. I keep replaying everything, blaming myself for not taking a different route that day. The guilt is a constant heavy weight, it just won’t lift. My memory is shot too; I’m forgetting meetings, where I put my keys – my team at work is noticing. And every little sound makes me jump out of my skin. The other day, a car horn made me drop my coffee. But it's not just that. Sometimes I hear whispers when no one's around, and I see things in my peripheral vision, quick flashes that aren’t there when I look directly. They don't seem to have anything to do with the accident, though. And then there are these really strange beliefs I've developed, things that I know aren't rational, but I can't shake them.
D018-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h006.question: It’s been almost a year since the accident in the ER, and I still can’t shake this feeling. I jump at every sudden movement, every unexpected face, my heart pounding like I’ve just run a marathon. I try to push away all the thoughts and memories from that night, but they’re always lurking. Sometimes my mind just goes blank, like a void, and I can't feel anything at all, good or bad – it's like a defense mechanism. I can remember bits and pieces of the chaotic scene, but other parts are just gone, a blurry mess. What’s really gotten to me lately are these… experiences. I hear whispers, see shadows at the edges of my vision, things that aren’t connected to the ER at all. They’re just *there*, like a separate, unsettling reality that accompanies everything else. It's making me so on edge, so irritable, like my nerves are frayed.
D018-D005_h006.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h007.question:
It's like my mind is playing tricks on me. I've been a wedding photographer for years, used to being the calm one, but lately, it's just… different. I keep seeing things, really vivid, almost like they're right there, not related to the accident at all. Just last week, during a ceremony, I saw a distorted face leering from behind the altar, clear as day even though no one was there. My husband tries to comfort me, but I just feel hollow. It’s been almost seven months now, and I can't even remember most of what happened during that car crash. It's like my memory just goes blank.

I also find myself flying off the handle for no reason. The other day, a sudden movement from a waiter made me jump, and I yelled at him, completely irrational. I just feel so on edge, so wary of everything. And the worst part is, sometimes I just feel like I'm not really here. It's like I'm watching my life from outside, especially when I try to think about the accident. I just… can't. And my husband, my family… I know I should feel something, love, affection, but it's like a switch has been flipped off. I just feel numb, completely numb around them, and it scares me.
D018-D005_h007.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h008.question:
It’s been almost a year since… that incident. I keep having these awful dreams, not exactly about what happened, but they leave me shaking like I’m back there, even if the dream content is totally different. During the day, my mind just goes blank whenever I try to think about some parts of it, specific moments are just… gone, like a missing scene in a film, even though I can recall other bits fine.

Lately, though, things have gotten really strange. I’ve started hearing things, voices whispering, sometimes even full conversations. They don’t talk about the incident at all, though. It’s usually rambling about things that make no sense, or sometimes they just repeat words over and over. And I’ve started to feel really… numb. I look at my family, my friends, and it’s like the love I used to feel for them isn’t there anymore, just a hollow space.

I also can't seem to control my temper. The smallest things set me off, and I just start yelling, saying things I regret. And if someone startles me, my heart races like crazy, my hands shake, and it takes ages for me to calm down. It all feels so disconnected, like pieces of a puzzle that just don't fit together, especially these voices that have nothing to do with what happened to me.
D018-D005_h008.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h009.question:
It's been… I don't even know how long, but things just aren't right. After the divorce, my mind started playing tricks on me. Sometimes, I’ll be teaching a class and suddenly, I’m not in the studio anymore. I’m back in that courtroom, reliving every painful moment, even though I try really hard not to think about it. It’s like I’m seeing it all happen again, right in front of me, but it's not even the worst part.

Lately, I’ve been hearing things. Not voices related to my ex or anything about the divorce, but strange whispers, sometimes music that isn't really there. And the other day, I was convinced I saw a shadowy figure standing in my apartment, watching me, but when I blinked, it was gone. It’s not like the flashbacks, which are about the past. These new things feel different, totally separate from what happened with my husband. It gets so overwhelming, I lashed out at a student this week for just bumping into me. And loud noises? Someone just walking into the room too fast will make me jump out of my skin. I also can't remember most of what happened during the divorce itself, just a big blank. And it feels like I can't feel anything good anymore, just a dull emptiness.
D018-D005_h009.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h010.question:
It’s hard to pinpoint when things really started going south, but for a while now, I’ve been feeling really off. I'm a detective, so I've seen my share of tough stuff, but this is different. Sometimes, I’ll be on a case, or even just at home with my wife, and suddenly I’m back there, feeling like I’m reliving a past shoot-out or a terrible accident. I’ll start acting like it’s happening again, my heart pounding, just like it did that day.

I've also been avoiding certain parts of the city, not because they're dangerous, but because they remind me of cases that got to me. It's like my memory of those events is all fuzzy in parts; I can recall some details clearly, but others are just blank, like a file with missing pages. Even with a good arrest or a solved case, there’s no satisfaction anymore; it just feels hollow. And recently, I’ve started lashing out, throwing things, yelling at people. The other day, I startled easily, and my heart was racing for hours. The worst part, though, is the voices. I hear them talking to me, sometimes even seeing things that aren't there – shadows in my peripheral vision, quick glimpses of faces. It’s not like they're telling me to relive a specific traumatic event, they're just… there, and it’s been happening more often.
D018-D005_h010.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h011.question:
"Lately, it's been getting harder and harder to focus on my mixing, especially with the constant noise. I'll be trying to EQ a track, and suddenly I hear voices, like a whole crowd murmuring things that aren't there. It's not like a flashback to some specific bad event, these voices are just... random, sometimes accusing me of things that make no sense, sometimes just unsettling chatter. It’s not about the car accident I was in a few months back, these sounds just started on their own.

When I’m out, I find myself actively trying to steer clear of certain areas of the city, especially the busier spots, because even the thought of running into certain people, or just the general vibe of those places, makes me incredibly uneasy. I just can't deal with it.

It's like my brain has just decided the whole world is a hostile place, that everyone is out to get something from me or judge me. I had a huge blow-up with my bandmate last week because I was convinced he was intentionally messing with my equipment. I just yelled at him, saying he always tries to sabotage my work. It felt like I couldn't stop myself. My life just feels meaningless sometimes."
D018-D005_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h012.question:
"It's been... I don't even know how long anymore. More than six months, definitely. I keep seeing things, usually faces, sometimes distorted animals right in my office or at home. They're not connected to anything that's happened to me, just... there. And the thoughts that come with them, like my own mind is playing tricks on me.

I try to keep to myself now. Going to work is a nightmare – the corridors, the bustling students, it all just makes me feel on edge, like I need to get away from everything and everyone. I find myself lashing out, too. A few weeks ago, I actually threw a stapler across my office because a student was just asking about admissions requirements, and I felt this uncontrollable surge of anger. Afterward, I just feel this immense guilt, but it’s like my mind isn't my own anymore. No one else understands that the world feels completely dangerous to me, or how meaningless everything has become. It's not because of any one event; it’s just the constant state I'm in."
D018-D005_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h013.question: Lately, it feels like my mind is playing tricks on me, and it’s been going on for a while now, more than six months. Even when I’m just trying to relax, I’ll hear muffled voices, sometimes whispering my name, even when no one is around. It’s not like they're talking about the gruesome scenes I clean up, just random things that don’t make sense, and it’s getting harder to ignore them. I guess I've also just started to believe that the world out there is completely dangerous, like there's no real meaning to anything. I try to push away all the thoughts about the things I’ve seen, the faces, the smells, but they just circle back. There have also been a few times, when I've just snapped, throwing things and yelling – once, I even broke my neighbor's window because I thought he was trying to break into my place. It isn't good. I can’t help but think that all this is my fault, that I could have done something to prevent the tragedies I encounter, even though I logically know I couldn't.
D018-D005_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h014.question: Lately, I’ve been feeling so on edge, it's like a constant hum of anxiety. I jump at every little noise at work, and if a car backfires outside, my heart practically leaps out of my chest. I try my best not to think about what happened in the past, pushing those memories away, but it's like they're always lurking. I sometimes feel like the world is a dangerous place, and sometimes I blame myself for how everything unfolded, like I could have done something differently. The other day, I threw my pen across the room during a particularly frustrating moment, something I regret. But what’s really been getting to me, for the past six months or so, are these voices. They whisper and sometimes even shout my name, and I see things—shadows moving in my peripheral vision, even when there's nothing there. It's so unsettling. These visions and voices have nothing to do with what happened to me; they're just… there. And sometimes, I feel like people are watching me, talking about me.
D018-D005_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h015.question:
"Honestly, doctor, it's been getting worse since my husband passed, about eight months now. I keep seeing things, usually shadows flitting at the edge of my vision, or I hear my late husband's voice calling my name, clear as day, even though I know he's gone. It's not like I'm reliving his accident; these things just happen.

And don't get me started on how I see the world now. It feels utterly meaningless, like what’s the point in anything when life is so fragile and dangerous? I blame myself for so much of it, for not doing more, for… everything. I try my best to push away these constant thoughts and pictures that pop into my head, but they just keep coming back. Sometimes, it’s all so overwhelming, I just lash out at anyone who tries to talk to me. I'm embarrassed to admit it, but I’ve been yelling at the cashier at the grocery store, cursing them out over nothing. It’s not like me at all."
D018-D005_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h016.question:
It's been about seven months now since the incident, and things just aren't right. I'm usually a steady man, dependable, especially with my job driving the underground; you have to be. But lately, memories of that jumper on the tracks just keep flooding back. I try to push them away, block them out, but they’re always there, playing over and over.

The worst part is what I'm seeing and hearing. I know it sounds mad, but I hear voices sometimes, whispers, telling me things that don’t make sense, things that have nothing to do with what happened on the tracks. And I see things too, shadows moving, figures in my peripheral vision that vanish when I turn my head. It started around the same time this whole nightmare did. When I'm working, I find myself constantly looking around, checking every corner of the station, the platform, like there's always danger lurking, even when it's just my regular run. My wife says I've changed, that I'm always on edge. I also find myself blaming dispatch, or even the signal operations, for somehow allowing the incident to happen, if only they had acted differently.
D018-D005_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h017.question:
It’s been months now, probably close to eight, since things really started going downhill. I’ve noticed myself actively steering clear of certain parts of the city, especially the area where… well, where that incident happened. Even just the thought of driving by makes my stomach clench. And if I see someone who even remotely looks like him, I get this intense jolt, like I'm right back there.

The worst part is, I keep seeing things, hearing things. Not like flashbacks, where I’m reliving it – these are different. Sometimes I hear whispers, even when no one’s there, or see shadows moving in my peripheral vision that disappear when I focus. They’re never about the incident; they're just... there. It’s gotten to the point where I’m constantly doing perimeter checks, sizing up every new face, even in my own apartment. I find myself checking the locks multiple times before bed, convinced someone might get in, even though there’s no rational reason for it. I also keep replaying how I could have done things differently during that job, blaming myself for what happened and feeling like I should’ve prevented it. It’s like my mind is playing tricks on me, and it’s exhausting.
D018-D005_h017.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h018.question:
"It's been a rough few months, doc. Ever since that incident at the bank, I just can't shake it. I keep seeing their faces, the masked men, flashing in my mind, even when I'm trying to relax. I try to push those thoughts away, tell myself it’s over, but they just… intrude. And honestly, it really ticks me off, because if management had just listened to my warnings about the security loopholes, none of this would have happened.

Lately, though, it’s gotten weirder. I’ve started hearing things, whispers mostly, sometimes like people talking about me when no one’s there. And sometimes the whispers accuse me of things that make no sense, like I’m some kind of spy for the robbers. These voices, they don't have anything to do with the robbery; they feel completely separate. I also sometimes think my wife is secretly recording me. It's making it hard to trust anyone. I’m always on edge, constantly checking every corner, every shadow, especially at work. I just don't know what's real anymore."
D018-D005_h018.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h019.question: Lately, things have been really tough, Dr. I keep having these vivid flashes, not just memories, but like I'm right back in the OR during that really difficult surgery where we lost the patient. It replays over and over, sometimes even when I'm just trying to relax. It's gotten so bad that I actively avoid anything – even discussions about similar cases or certain hallways in the hospital – that might trigger those awful feelings. I also can't shake this feeling that it was the attending physician's fault, that if they had just followed my suggestions, things would have been different. I find myself constantly checking my surroundings, like scanning exits and observing everyone in the room, just in case something unexpected happens. But the weirdest part is I also hear voices, often whispering my name or sometimes saying odd, unrelated things about me. These aren't tied to the surgery; they just… appear. It's been going on for a little over six months now.
D018-D005_h019.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h020.question: It’s been months since everything changed, right after that awful accident. I keep seeing it all play out in my head, especially when I'm trying to sleep. It’s like a movie I can't turn off, just replaying the screams and the metal crunching. I try so hard not to think about it, to push all those feelings away, but it’s always there, lurking. And I know it was my fault, completely. If I had just done something differently. Lately, though, it’s gotten weirder. I’ve been hearing voices when no one’s around, whispering things that have nothing to do with what happened in the accident, just strange comments about me, sometimes telling me to do things. I also caught myself looking over my shoulder constantly, checking all the exits, even when I'm just at the library or walking down a quiet street. I feel like someone is watching me, but it's not connected to the accident. It’s a totally different kind of fear, separate from all the trauma from before.
D018-D005_h020.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h021.question:
Lately, things have just felt… off. It’s been about seven or eight months now. I’m a bus driver, you know, been doing it for years, always enjoyed meeting new people. But now, getting on that bus… sometimes I hear things. Not related to the accident I was in last year, not like reliving the crash or anything, but just voices, mumbling, sometimes saying my name. It often feels like the other passengers are talking about me, too, even when I know they can’t be. It’s not just the voices; my mind feels like it’s playing tricks on me in other ways, like my thoughts aren't fully my own.

I’m also just… not myself. It’s hard to feel any kind of joy anymore, even when my wife tries to cheer me up or when the grandkids visit. I just feel this deep shame, like I’m a failure, like everything that happened is somehow my fault. It makes me angry sometimes, when I hear those things or just feel so dead inside. I find myself yelling at my wife, or even at passengers, over tiny things on the bus, just cussing them out without thinking. I’m not proud of it. And then, seeing anything that reminds me of that accident, like a certain intersection or even just the smell of exhaust, it just fills me with an intense dread, a feeling I can’t explain.
D018-D005_h021.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D005_h022.question:
"Well, I’m 62, and my husband keeps telling me I need to talk to someone. It’s been… a while now, probably close to eight months. I’ve been having these dreams, almost every night. They’re not about the accident specifically, not directly, but they’re just unsettling, full of strange images and voices that leave me feeling awful when I wake up. And then during the day, it's this constant knot in my stomach, like something terrible is always about to happen. Even when things are going right, like when I finish my census work and get all the forms perfect, there’s no real feeling of accomplishment, just… emptiness.

But the most disturbing thing is these voices. I hear them talking to me, sometimes arguing, sometimes saying quite nasty things. They're not connected to what happened during the accident, not like reliving it. They just appear, interjecting themselves into my day, totally out of the blue, making comments about what I’m doing or seeing. And sometimes, these voices get so loud or so critical that I just… lash out. I’ve broken a few dishes and even yelled at my neighbor once, which is completely unlike me. It’s like another presence is there, separate from anything I’ve ever experienced, and it has nothing to do with that memory."
D018-D005_h022.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D005_h023.question:
It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when things started going downhill, but it’s been months, maybe even close to a year now. Driving the subway, especially in the tunnels, has become a nightmare. Every time I get into that cabin, I feel this intense dread, like something awful is about to happen.

It’s not just the feeling; I hear things, too. Whispers, mumbling coming from the empty passenger cars, sometimes even voices arguing about me. They’re not connected to anything that’s ever happened down there. They just… are. And then there are the shadows, moving just out of sight in my peripheral vision, almost like people are lurking on the tracks even when I know they can't be. These sounds and sights aren’t like a flashback of something I’ve experienced, they’re just... there.

I'm constantly seething with anger. Every little thing sets me off. Just yesterday, a car pulled out in front of me and I just saw red. I ended up smashing my phone. Even when I manage to get through a shift without incident, there’s no satisfaction, no feeling of a job well done. It’s like a hollow accomplishment. All I know is, these voices, these visions, they’re making me question everything, and they definitely aren’t about some past trauma.
D018-D005_h023.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D005_h024.question: It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when things started feeling off, but for about eight months now, my life has been... fractured. I’m a 44-year-old architect, and normally I thrive on order, but now, everything feels chaotic. My heart races and I start sweating whenever I see a certain type of scaffolding, or even just hear a sudden, loud bang, which reminds me of a workplace accident I witnessed a while back. I’m constantly on edge, consumed by a gnawing fear that something terrible is about to happen, even when things are going well. Even when a building design gets approved, or I meet a tough deadline, there's no real satisfaction, it just feels empty. The worst part is the voices and images. I hear whispers, often telling me that my designs are flawed or that people are talking about me behind my back. Sometimes I see shadows darting in my periphery. These things, they aren't tied to the accident at all; they just started happening on their own, and it's making me lash out. Lately, I've completely lost my temper and thrown things at the wall, and even gotten into a shouting match with a colleague last week. I know it’s not right, but it's like I'm not myself anymore.
D018-D005_h024.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D005_h025.question:
Lately, my sleep’s been a battlefield. I keep reliving the accident on the shipyard – the crane collapsing, the metal screeching, everything. It’s always the same, and I wake up in a cold sweat, my heart pounding. It’s hard to feel good about anything anymore. Even after we finished the last hull ahead of schedule, I just felt… flat. No pride, no relief, just the same gnawing dread. This constant fear is exhausting. I’m always on edge, always expecting something else to go wrong.

And then there are the voices. They've been around for months now, sometimes whispering, sometimes a full-blown argument right in the room with me.
